messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: inference-high-latency — p95 spike on text-gen in us-west-2. Paging @Elinor (oncall). Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/inference/high-latency
Elinor (oncall): got it, ack. Looking now.
Elinor (oncall): quick status — dashboards show p50 up ~120ms -> 400ms and p95 > 1.2s across model-neo-3b variants. No full 5xx surge, mostly timeouts and some TCP retries.
Sam (SRE): I'm seeing a pattern of KV-cache eviction thrash on the embedder/kv nodes around 12:05 UTC; eviction job kicked at 12:01 with aggressive ttl of 30s. Logs: ```evict: shard=12 removing 384 keys took 3.1s
evict: shard=8 removing 410 keys took 2.9s
...
request_latency: vm=pool-a instance=task-22 tail=1.3s```
Jordan (Infra): the autoscaler bumped pool-b at 12:02 but backing infra throttled new containers for ~90s, so we had a capacity gap.
Marta (CSE): heads-up — two enterprise customers (acme-corp, nova-ai) opened support tickets around 12:07 complaining about slow responses in production. Minimal data loss but degraded UX.
Elinor (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) roll back eviction TTL to previous value 2) temporarily pin routing to older model variant with smaller kv footprint 3) scale up pool-a by +2 nodes manually. Doing 1 now.
Elinor (oncall): rollback TTL -> set to 600s (from 30s). Command: ```# set eviction ttl
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS" https://controlplane/api/kv/config -d '{"ttl_seconds":600}'```
ops-bot: action: config_change detected by Elinor — eviction.ttl set to 600s (change-id: cfg-20260315-01).
Sam (SRE): After TTL rollback, p50/p95 trending back down but still elevated. I recommend pressing routing fallback to the smaller-ram variant for the busiest endpoints for ~10m. I can push that if Jordan agrees.
Jordan (Infra): agree. Kicking canary route to model-neo-3b-small for 20% traffic on /v1/generate for 5m. Command: ```rbctl route set --route /v1/generate --model neo-3b-small --weight 20 --duration 5m```
Marta (CSE): I've told support to notify acme-corp and nova-ai that we saw transient latency, mitigation in progress; SLA impact metric to be provided postmortem.
Kai (EngPM): schedule quick post-incident sync at 15:00 UTC to capture timeline and action items. Who owns the postmortem writeup?
Elinor (oncall): I'll capture the initial timeline + mitigation steps; Sam can add SRE analysis; Jordan will add infra root cause; Kai to review and finalize.
Sam (SRE): initial assessment: probable root cause = overly aggressive KV eviction TTL + autoscaler configuration gap causing simultaneous cache thrash and capacity shortfall -> request amplification and higher tail latency. Need data to confirm (evictions per shard, request fanout).
Jordan (Infra): infra follow-up: investigate autoscaler cooldown/queueing for pool-b with cloud provider (rate limit on node attach) and add a guard to avoid aggressive scaling in presence of evictions.
Kai (EngPM): action items (assign, severity, estimate):
- A1: Add synthetic canary for KV eviction behavior on rolling configs (owner: Sam) | severity: Sev3 | estimate: 3d | quarter: Q2 reliability OKR
- A2: Harden autoscaler backoff & node attach retries (owner: Jordan) | severity: Sev2 | estimate: 5d | quarter: Q2 infra resilience
- A3: Create routing fallback playbook + automatic canary rollout on high latency (owner: Elinor) | severity: Sev3 | estimate: 2d | quarter: Q2 runbook improvements
- A4: Customer impact report and SLA math + support comms template (owner: Marta) | severity: Sev4 | estimate: 1d | quarter: Q2 CS readiness
Kai (EngPM): Priority: A2 > A1 ~= A3 > A4. Tie A2/A1 to quarterly sprint lane for reliability (map to story epic REL-2026-Q2).
Elinor (oncall): created Jira: https://jira.internal/browse/REL-2026-321 (A2), REL-2026-322 (A1), REL-2026-323 (A3), REL-2026-324 (A4). Adding owners.
Sam (SRE): sizing notes: A1 needs a small harness + baseline metrics: estimate 3 engineer-days (1 exploratory + 2 for infra + tests). A2 touches cloud APIs, might need 2 engineers + infra approval for provider quota bump, estimate 5-7 days.
Jordan (Infra): will draft proposal for autoscaler change and schedule a provider sync. Blocking: provider quota check and infra change window.
Marta (CSE): I'll prepare customer impact summary and assign to support for templated comms. Prioritize acme-corp ticket for rollback notice.
ops-bot: handoff: oncall shift change at 14:00 UTC — @Elinor handing to @Jordan (Infra) for post-mitigation monitoring window. Summary: TTL rollback, routing canary, manual +2 nodes to pool-a.
Jordan (Infra): taking over monitoring. I'll keep the routing weight at 20% for 10m and then ramp down once p95 < 500ms for 10m window.
Elinor (oncall): any objections to closing pager after monitoring window?
Sam (SRE): let's keep pager open until we have 30m of stable metrics, then close.
Kai (EngPM): postmortem sprint tie-in: please add estimated effort to each ticket and tag with quarter tag 'Q2-Reliability'. We'll review in engineering priorities sync on Monday to ensure resourcing.
Marta (CSE): schedule note — I'll join the Monday sync to discuss customer comms timing.
Elinor (oncall): final note: saved logs and heap profiles pushed to s3://redwood-incident/1767007777/; retention 30d. Link: https://s3.console/internal/redwood-incident/1767007777/
ops-bot: incident-bot: status changed to "mitigated" by Elinor at 12:32 UTC.
Sam (SRE): closing monitoring window now, p95 stable ~320ms, p99 occasional spikes at 600ms but low volume. Good to proceed with action item work.
Jordan (Infra): I updated REL-2026-321 with provider checklist and requested quota review.
Kai (EngPM): thanks everyone. Postmortem doc draft request: please add initial timeline and raw metrics to the doc by EOD. I'll set the postmortem meeting invite and include stakeholders from SRE, Infra, DevEx, and CS.
Marta (CSE): note to add customer impact labels to Jira tickets for prioritization.
Elinor (oncall): handing off formally. Good job team. :thumbsup:
